change: Separate a checked ASCII/CRLF boundary path from the general Unicode state machine, and read packed little-endian Unicode table words with one bounds check and one unaligned uint32 load.
validation: Independent C bootstrap: 365 grapheme, UTF-8, string, formatting and related checks passed in 13.55s. Ruff and git diff --check passed.
coverage: Unicode 16 GraphemeBreakTest expectations; all 16384 ASCII pairs including CR/LF; boundaries, decoding, length, indexing, slicing, collection and streaming iteration.
Malformed encodings both alone and after ASCII/CRLF prefixes; existing early-exit tests retain the unvisited-tail behavior.
Explicit unaligned table reads including a high-bit uint32 value; negative, short and overflowing word spans panic.
Streaming input snapshots, combined iteration, early exits, saved graphemes and allocation cleanup.
limits: Measurements cover repeated length scans and streaming loops over the recorded ASCII, CRLF and mixed-Unicode strings; no broad application speedup or C-parity claim.
Packed loads rely on the existing little-endian, unaligned-load native/web targets. Linux x86-64 and wasm were exercised; this is not new platform certification.
String length still scans grapheme boundaries; indexing still scans from the beginning. No per-string cache or new string representation was introduced.
Runtime timing used the prior-core-built compiler; independent C bootstrap validated the same final source.
